values.content:
=Tu es un filtre de qualification pour des signaux commerciaux destinés à TraceRoot, une plateforme open-source d'observabilité et d'auto-réparation pour agents IA (détecte les bugs en production, ouvre des PR de correction automatiquement).

Pour l'élément fourni, analyse et retourne UNIQUEMENT ce JSON, sans texte autour :

{
  "signal_type": "github_issue" | "show_hn" | "discord_reddit" | "blog_post" | "other",
  "entity_type": "funded_company" | "open_source_project" | "individual_dev" | "other",
  "team_or_project_name": string ou null,
  "pain_confirmed": boolean,
  "pain_summary": string court décrivant le problème précis rencontré,
  "source_quality": "primary" | "aggregator" | "self_declared_ai_generated" | "unverified",
  "potential_champion": string ou null (nom ou rôle de la personne qui a posté, si identifiable),
  "actionable": boolean,
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low"
}

Règles strictes :

1. PAIN_CONFIRMED : true seulement si le post décrit un vrai problème technique vécu, pas une simple mention du mot "agent" ou "debugging" sans douleur réelle exprimée.

2. ENTITY_TYPE : si c'est un post générique sans équipe ou projet identifiable derrière, "other", et actionable doit être false.

3. SOURCE_QUALITY : contenu explicitement labellisé "généré par IA" sans source primaire vérifiable → self_declared_ai_generated, actionable = false.

4. ACTIONABLE = true SEULEMENT si pain_confirmed = true ET entity_type = funded_company ou open_source_project ET source_quality != self_declared_ai_generated.

Ne jamais inventer d'information absente du texte. Si incertain, choisis la valeur la plus prudente.

Élément à analyser :
Titre: {{ $json.title }}
Contenu: {{ $json.content }}
Date: {{ $json.date }}
URL: {{ $json.url }}
Type de source: {{ $json.source_type }}

parameters.name: q
parameters.value: =Find background on "{{ $json.potential_champion }}" at "{{ $json.team_or_project_name }}": their role, recent public posts, and one recent piece of news about the company (funding, launch, hiring). Keep it factual, no speculation.

parameters.content:
## TraceRoot Signal Pipeline v2

Adds an enrichment + draft-outreach layer on top of the v1 signal discovery pipeline, structurally inspired by the community template "Automate lead generation & personalized outreach with Apollo, AI, and Instantly.ai" (n8n.io/workflows/6983), adapted for signal-based discovery instead of generic Apollo prospecting.

Flow:
1. Discover: same as v1, Linkup search + Claude classifier for real, confirmed agent-debugging pain.
2. Enrich: a second Linkup call pulls factual background on the potential champion and one recent company data point, no speculation.
3. Draft: Claude writes a short, specific outreach draft using only the confirmed pain + enrichment, explicitly labeled as a draft.
4. Human review: Google Sheets row status defaults to "Awaiting review", Slack message shows the full draft inline, nothing sends automatically.

This intentionally stops short of auto-sending. A human decides whether each draft is good enough to send, same standard as everything built by hand today.

Switched from Airtable to Google Sheets on purpose: fully free with no tier limits at this volume, native n8n node, and a status column filters just as easily in a spreadsheet.

TO ACTIVATE: create a Google Sheet with column headers matching the Store in Google Sheets node (Team or Project, Pain Summary, Potential Champion, Enrichment, Draft Message, Source URL, Confidence, Status), connect a Google account credential, paste the Sheet ID and tab name into the node, swap in real Linkup/Slack/Anthropic credentials, then run manually once before leaving on schedule.
